questions.question: Does CtCommand3P(actor,title,desc) take actor: "A"|"B"|"C", and does check(m) return true only when m.actorIsMember(actor) && m.groupId !== null? Cite the constructor and check body.
Does UtCommand3P(actor,title) accept the three-actor type and assert the post-update task title via r.getTask(actor, ...) in run()? Cite the run postcondition.
Does ScCommand3P(actor,status) assert status-enum closure post-dispatch (the A2 per-command postcondition)? Cite the assertion.
Does AsCommand3P(actor) take actor and assert its assignment postcondition (A4) mirroring the 2-party form? Cite the assertion.
Does UnCommand3P(actor) take actor and assert assignee===null post-dispatch (A5)? Cite the assertion.
Does DtCommand3P(actor) take actor and assert the deleted task is absent post-dispatch? Cite the assertion.
Does RlCommand3P(actor) take actor and assert task persistence after reload (A11) mirroring the 2-party form? Cite the assertion.
Does every command's toString() return `${actor}.Verb(args)` matching the matrix DSL (e.g. C.Ct(title), B.Sc(open))? Cite each toString().
Do all task commands dispatch on the acting actor's own page (r.page(actor)) and read postconditions from that same actor's page, never hard-coding pageA?
Do the check() preconditions that require an existing task (Ut/Sc/As/Un/Dt) also gate on m.tasks.size > 0 so fast-check prunes impossible commands rather than failing at run time?
Are the 3-party command classes self-contained in the new file (no edits to e2e/tests/multi-user.property.spec.ts and no changes to two-party.ts signatures)?

Are MLS commit/dispatch errors that are non-actionable (e.g. transient epoch races) handled the same way as the 2-party file (try/catch that skips postconditions) rather than failing the property run spuriously?
